utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we then please pull back the map so that I can show you that in fact it is the same location. Well, first of all, I'd like to tender this into evidence, and then if we can get the map back on the screens, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That will be Exhibit D639. Would you like to bring back the marked map or the clean map?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The marked map, please. D638. D638.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, will this be of assistance? We can see Zagrici, the cemetery, and Baba Stijena. Is that approximately on the same line as we can see in the map and also in the photo?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: If -- if possible, I would like to explain something about maps. This is a city map and this is not -- for precise terrain features, I would need a topographical map, because a terrain -- a city map is only to guide people to a certain street. And a topographical map represents exactly the -- the features. But I would like to state that from direction 3 to line -- to 1, it can be -- oh, sorry. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. I will ask the usher to help the witness. Would you like to mark the map again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would like to draw something on there, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Just -- could you wait a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the meantime, Mr. Van der Weijden, can you just tell us whether this was the direction of fire? Was it along this line, the line that actually goes through these various features?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll hear from the witness. Why don't you use black colour this time. Yes, Mr. Van der Weijden.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From my findings, the only direction that is -- that is possible, it's - I'll try to draw it as straight as possible - is from 3 to 1. But since in the picture that I've -- where I've marked the Muslim cemetery, I do not see if it's the complete cemetery. So it might indeed be this line, which would not be visible from the house. So I would have a sight on the house, but it's different. The photo that shows the Muslim cemetery is not exactly from the same location where the victim was hit. So it's not possible to -- for me to conclude if -- if it would be possible to be fired upon from the cemetery as well. It really is important that even 50 centimetre or a metre distance can change the whole tactical situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we give this a separate number, or shall we keep it as is? Let me consult with the court deputy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will give this a separate number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is Exhibit D640, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please get 1D0247. I apologise. 1D02407.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This will be a magnified portion of the area where the cemetery is in order to assist you to better orientate yourself and determine the direction more easily. Is this a view of the cemetery from Zagrici Street, the cemetery that you marked?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I do recognise on the extreme left the -- the right side of the house that was visible in the previous photos, but I do know -- I do not know from which exact location the picture was taken. But that is the Muslim cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, if I can be of assistance, let me just say that this is the same photograph -- or, rather, the same location as earlier, except here it is zoomed in on. So we only see the last two houses in the row and the cemetery in the background. Would you agree with me? And the electric power line runs along Zagrici Street; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I would not be able to conclude that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we need to bring back the earlier photo so that you can see the whole photo and then to show you -- so you can compare this blow-up with the original photograph? And the house on the right, as you can see from the earlier photograph, is in fact the house where the incident was.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it possible to split the screen and have the two photos one next to the other, please? D6309 and the one that we have before us. Could we please show D639 together with the photograph that we have on the left screen, on the right-hand side of the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, would you agree with me that you can see in the background the two houses that are zoomed in on the right-hand photograph and that it is the same position exactly except that we have a magnified and enlarged portion of the photograph on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please put your -- your initials and the date on the right-hand-side photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. There's no need for the witness doing that. We'll just admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D641, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now please have 1D02408.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, can we agree that this is a view of the area from the hill on the opposite side, from the northern slope? And can you locate the cemetery and Baba Stijena and draw a line to connect the two to show the path of the bullet to the location of the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. Could -- could I request that the accused put his questions one by one to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. If Mr. Van der Weijden could mark the -- the position of Baba Rock and Muslim cemetery and then draw a line of the projectile.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, this picture was taken from a location that I haven't visited. This is on the opposite side of the town. I would need a map to exactly pinpoint the locations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you locate the place of incident from this -- from this photo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not like this. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But can you -- can you locate the place which is called Baba Rock?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know it's one -- one of the rocks here on top, but I would -- I would really need a map to exactly locate them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In that case, perhaps I can ask Mr. Van der Weijden to take a look at a map. And then with the assistance of the map, perhaps he can be assisted in drawing the line between Baba Rock and the location of the incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The map Mr. Van der Weijden refers to is a map with topographical assistance, I take it. Will that be of any assistance, Mr. Van der Weijden?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will try. Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Just for the record, Your Honours, the map Mr. Van der Weijden has in his hand is the street map. It doesn't have topographical features.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON

utterances.text: The area 1 would be where Baba Rock would be located, within that area. Not -- it's not possible to precisely point it out, but I know -- I remember that it's between the big building and the high rock on the -- or the high cliff on the right side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, I imagine it's feasible, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you told about that, anything about that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I was told that Baba Rock was controlled by the VRS, and for the rest I have no information about where the separation line was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, if I tell you that right below the road which is in the upper third of your circle, so right below your road, the line of separation was - would you accept it if I said that to you? - and that this area was under the Muslim control?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I would not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It would be of assistance both to you and to us. Thank you. Would you please put your initials and the date.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. This marked photo will be admitted as Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D642, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now please have 1D02403.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.text: It's a Google Earth photograph, and maybe that will assist you in determining the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this of any assistance?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you see that this shorter parameter is 870 metres, and if we were to go across the cemetery, then it would be even longer, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. The -- the photograph being shown to the witness at the moment doesn't indicate where the 870 metres ends. And Mr. Karadzic, again, he's talking about the cemetery, and he hasn't elicited any evidence as to where the cemetery is in relation to this particular photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Agreed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see the cemetery in this photo, Mr. Van der Weijden?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that Zagrici Street, which we can see here, is open, facing the cemetery, and that that is the direction leading to Baba Rock; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The street itself is open, facing the cemetery. I would conclude that from this -- from this picture. But I would not know exactly because I would have to check on -- on the incident site itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And where in reference to Zagrici Street is Baba Rock?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But first of all let us establish whether witness is able to mark the place where the incident allegedly took place. Can you do that? Oh.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could -- yes. Just wait a second, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh, it moved. It zoomed in.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's -- now the exact location has disappeared to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't you zoom out one further.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Left --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, it's -- well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's again -- so the incident site as I've marked with blue, that's where the incident took place, between the houses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the Muslim cemetery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would be this area, this area, and some of this area, from what I see here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So what is your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree, then, that the line marked with 870 metres actually indicates the direction where in continuation we would have Baba Rock?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I have not drawn that exact line, so I would not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please date and initial this photograph.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I have to note that these are all waste of time. This --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, we will show that there was no chance of the fire coming from Baba Stijena or Baba Rock. And we will go step-by-step, because in the next photo we will show Baba Rock from which you cannot see either the cemetery or the incident site. I would like to tender this photo, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D643, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have 1D02404.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that this is the location of Baba Stijena, Baba Rock, the location from which the photo was taken?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I only know the general location of Baba Rock, so I cannot conclude this from this photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Have you been to Baba Rock, and have you made any photos from there of your own?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I have been to a location where I think the shot has originated from, and I was told -- I was pointed in a -- in a general direction that that was Baba Rock by -- by one of the witnesses and the investigator. So I do not know if Baba Rock is within a few metre parameter or it's a wider feature, a bigger feature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it possible that they misled you and maybe took you to some other location and said that that was Baba Rock?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: They did not take me to any location because I went to the location that -- where I wanted to go, because that was the location where I think the shell originated from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And you took a picture from that place.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Which is appearing on your report, page 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see this house on the right-hand side? That's the same house that we could see in the earlier photo but taken from the hill on the opposite side. Are these -- the buildings that are here that we see on the right-hand side of the photo, are these the buildings that we saw on the earlier photograph?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Well, I do recognise some of the buildings, only this picture was taken -- taken in a year where the trees had leaves. And both the incidents, at the time of the incident and the time of my visit, the trees were without leaves, which would heavily influence the visibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you do not question that this is a direction from which, in your view, the bullet had come -- could have come?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: From somewhere in this area, because it's not exactly the same position where I've taken the picture from, that would be the -- the origin of fire, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please date this, or perhaps we can just tender it as it is, depending on the Trial Chamber's view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But, Mr. Van der Weijden, can you locate the place of the -- that incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that -- not with this photo I can't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. No. Thank you. Any objections, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No. No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D644, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now please call 1D02-407. Thank you. This is just is to remind ourselves, but could we now have 1D02-405.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that there is only one road at the foothill of Baba, and is that the road that we are seeing in this photo?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: From both the map and the Google Earth view, there appears to be only one road leading up. There is a road that passes by Baba Stijena from east to west, but there is only one road leading from -- from north to south up to Baba.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have this photograph tendered into documents as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. This will be D645. 645, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, having looked at these photographs, there is no visibility, optical visibility, towards the Zagrici Street and the -- Zagrici Street and the Muslim cemetery. Do you see this elevation from which the Muslim cemetery can be seen?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'm sorry, objection. Could -- once again, it seems to be a compound question. Could the accused put each assertion to the witness to give him an opportunity to respond to each assertion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, let me be of assistance. Mr. Van der Weijden, this is viewed from the direction of Baba Rock. We agreed on that. Could you see anywhere the Muslim cemetery which is located between the Baba Rock and the incident site?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether witness agreed that this is a view from the Baba Rock.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is a view from -- from Baba Rock only maybe not exactly in the same location where I was standing, but this is a view more to the east. If I could have the previous picture, because I recognise some of the features.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you feature --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation] [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- both pictures at the same time. This is the difficulty with the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: From the left-hand-side photograph, or in that photograph, can you see the Muslim cemetery and the incident site? The previous one, D644.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I was referring actually to the other photo that was taken from Baba Rock. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D644.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that the one, Mr. Van der Weijden?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: This is the one. Could I have the left photograph on the full page, please. Slightly more, please. Yes, okay. Thank you. Could I -- can I draw? Because I can see on the picture that I have in my report on page 15, on the paper version, in the round -- the rounded-off photograph, this group of buildings is visible, the roofs, the red, green, and black roof, and down below in the distance this L-shaped building is also visible, which is in the exact line from where the shooter was that leads back to the position. So more or less the position is in the same -- that picture -- this picture was taken from the same location. And the location of the incident site would be somewhere in between. But like I said before, these trees now have leaves so that alters the visibility of the incident location. As visible in the picture on page 15, at the time that I visit, I did have a view on the location site of the incident site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you put the date and your signature.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now see page 15 of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be kept as --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we just put numbers to indicate what is what.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Circle number 1, number 2, and number 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sorry. Yes, if he's still working with this, I was going to ask that it be admitted, but.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we will admit it. Could you put number 1 on the place of the incident. Oops, we lost again, but we can mark it again. Could you put -- could you mark with number 1. That's ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay. Could you tell us what does number 1 refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Number 1 is the incident site, the general location of the incident site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And number 3?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Number 3 is the L-shaped building that's visible in the top of the photo on page 15 of the paper version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And number 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Number 2 is the roofs of the houses that are visible in the bottom of the photo on page 15 of the paper version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you put the date and the signature again, kindly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Perhaps just for the record, Mr. President, where the witness says the paper version, he's referring to the paper version of his expert report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I -- I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So we'll keep this as Exhibit D646. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before this is removed, can you mark the direction of the projectile trajectory and mark the position where the shooter was?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I cannot mark the location of the shooter because, again, I would have to be down at the ground level and to establish a position that would be suitable. And for the trajectory, the trajectory is not a straight line; it's a parabolic line. And I would have to know the exact calibre and rifle which was used to be able to establish that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If we bring back that marked picture again, could you roughly mark the direction of the fire on that -- we'll bring back D646. Just a second. Could you wait a minute.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The direction of fire would be where the arrow is pointed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll keep D646 as is now. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said in your previous answer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Just a second. I think we lost -- could you kindly mark -- he has to mark again the direction of fire. As you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It was saved. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that you didn't know the exact calibre and the type of weapon that was used to fire?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Van der Weijden, are you aware with the adjudicated facts cited by the OTP in connection with this incident? And these facts were adjudicated in the Galic case.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I have them listed in the -- in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that, starting from the beginning, 27, 32, several times, that what we have here is an evolution of the conclusion relating to the location of Baba Rock to the fact whether the weather was chilly and foggy and whether several shots were fired at unspecified time after he [as interpreted] daughter left to return home? Further on, it says that her mother had told her to take off her dirty shoes, which makes no sense because one cannot have dirty shoes when it is frosty. So do you know the weather conditions that prevailed in Sarajevo? In other words, that if there is the fog, then there is frost as well?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I did not know the weather conditions at the time of the incidents. But when I visited Sarajevo in November 2006, there was fog, but there was no frost. So it doesn't necessarily have to be freezing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please focus on paragraph -- paragraph 535, page 17, 17th paragraph: [In English] "Both parents believed that the bullet that had injured their daughter had been fired from a bridge known as Baba Stijena, because the location was visible from their house and was controlled by the SRK." [Interpretation] Was their yard visible only from the Baba Rock, or was the prevailing factor in the determination that this was controlled by the SRK? Or is it possible that it could have come from any other location, irrespective of who controlled it?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The complete yard might have be -- parts of the yard might have been visible from other locations, but the exact incident site at knee level, at leg level, so almost ground level, where the child was hit, from there, the area that they indicate as -- as Baba Rock was -- is the only possibility. There is a possibility that the shot might have come from 25 metres directly next to the street, because that's the only other option, but for me that was -- I ruled that out because of tactical reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could it have come from the cemetery or from any other point on the line between the incident site and the Baba Rock? How come that you did not conclude that it had come from another direction?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I would refer to the photo number 2 that I took from the incident site towards the location that I -- that I concluded the shot came from, which is on page 15 of my report, on the paper version. As you can see, there's only -- there is a possibility that it might have come from the house, on the foreground, but the only other possibility is from the upper rock. So the cemetery is not -- the cemetery does not have a view on the exact incident site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know the deployment of forces in Sirokaca where the Zagrici Street is?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you see that the cemetery was elevated and that the passage between the two houses can be seen from the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I agree that the passage between the two houses can be seen from the cemetery because we drove past the cemetery on the way to the top. I actually stopped at the cemetery to see if I could take a -- have a clear view of the incident site, but I did not, so I drove -- I had to drive higher up the mountain. So I can see the passage but not the actual incident site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you make a photo?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Not from the cemetery because I could not -- could not see it. I could not see the incident site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tell me what kind of wound one can expect to be sustained by a 3-year-old child by a 7.9 millimetre bullet?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It depends, of course, where the child was hit. In her case, in the right leg, because it's a relatively small mass for which the bullet will have to pass through, it will be an in-an-out shot. So there will be no tumbling of a bullet or a lot of transfer of energy. So the bullet will go in, it will go out. It will not have the same devastation as on an adult on the same location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, we'll have a break for half an hour. But bear that in mind, as I indicated earlier on, the -- this witness's evidence is of limited nature, and you don't have to go into detail, in such a detail to challenge the Prosecution's argument. You can deal with in general matter, in general matter, and you can deal with his method of such things, but -- and try to finish your cross-examination during the time set by the Chamber. And plan, again, your cross-examination during the break. We will resume --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the break, may I just ask the following: We do not have an investigator, nor will the investigator who did this will -- testify. The adjudicated facts are an integral part of this document. We have no other opportunity of disputing this because there is no truth about any of these incidents. So when is the Defence going to be given an opportunity to do that? My learned friends from the OTP are using this opportunity to pack an enormous number of facts into evidence that I have no chance to test or challenge. When else can I do that apart through this witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It is for you how to plan your defence strategy, but you have ample opportunity to bring your witnesses. We will resume at 35 past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, can you see among these adjudicated facts, for example, the description of how this idea evolved of the possibility of fire coming from Spicasta Stijena? That's page -- on page 17. The parents believed that it came from Spicasta Stijena because it was held by the SRK, and it says Anisa Pita was injured by a shot fired from the area of Baba Stijena. Do you have any evidence or any document that would corroborate this conclusion that she was wounded by a shot that came from Spicasta Stijena? What is the basis of your supporting this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The basis of my support to this conclusion is -- has been that I visited the incident site, checked what was technically possible for a bullet to end up in the victim or -- and then see from the tactical possibilities which possibilities would remain or would be removed because of tactical reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And which were the possibilities that you eliminated? Or let's better move to page 13 of your report. And I would ask everyone involved to pay attention to this page. The little girl Anisa Pita was wounded exactly in which part of her leg?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It only was -- says here that she was wounded in her right leg. So I don't know exactly which -- which part of her leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your report -- or, rather, in the adjudicated facts it says, and I'll find this place, "above the knee." Is it true that she was wounded above the knee, or was she wounded in the foot?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I do not know because the only information that I've had is that she was wounded in her right leg, as was written in the situation or as in the -- you've mentioned in the adjudicated facts that she was wounded in -- above the knee.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's see what else you concluded on page 13. "The calibre of the bullet that struck Anisa will not have been greater than 7.92 millimetres. Calibres greater than that would have caused far more serious damage than in this incident." What kind of injury was caused by this shot for which you presume must have been inflicted by 7.9 millimetres? Have you seen any related documents or have you seen the wound itself?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I reached my conclusion because I saw the -- where -- the victim. She was in the -- in the house at the time of my visit, and she still had both her legs. The calibre that would be above 7.92 millimetres that was available or that was present at the time was 12.7 millimetres, which probably would have -- most likely would have taken off her leg. So because she had two legs left, therefore I concluded that she had -- that the calibre must not have been greater than 7.92 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How does a entry/exit wound look like? Have you seen it?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I've seen entry and exit wounds, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In which part of the leg?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Oh, I have not seen for this case, but I have seen entry and exit wounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's go on. You have seen the child, but you didn't look at the wound. You saw the child, but you did not see the wound; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: And she wouldn't have been a child any longer, would she?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, she wouldn't. She's a teenager now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It goes on to say: "The standard assault rifle round, 6.6 -- 7.62x39 millimetre would have been at its extreme range and would be very inaccurate, so in my opinion there are three calibres that could have been used in this incident. These are: 7.62x51 millimetre, 54 millimetres, and 57 millimetres." Did the Serbian Army had any weapons of this type and these calibres?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The last one, the 57, is not -- does not work with 7.62. That is the 7.92 millimetres. But for the -- these calibres, at least the last two, the 54 and the 7.92x57, these were available to the Serbian army as they were to all the forces. As for the 7.62x51, that was a calibre that was produced in the republic -- in Yugoslavia before the war, mainly for export reasons. So they might be available to any forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And which weapons are used to fire these calibre rounds?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: For that I would have to refer to Annex A, which is the weapons. To Appendix A, weapons and ammunition. There I have listed which weapons work with what ammunition. And as you can see, that several weapons are suitable for more ammunition. If they were -- depending on -- for which round they were chambered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that 7.62x54 millimetres was the ammunition that we didn't have at all, what would you say to that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I found that -- I would find that very strange because I visited the Republic of Yugoslavia during the war, and I saw Serbian troops at check-points with weapons that fire 7.62x54R rounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you find in the requisition papers of the Army of Republika Srpska any indication that this type of ammunition was procured?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I was not given requisition papers of the Serbian army for my investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to paragraph 3 on your page 13. The distance that you estimated was 920 metres; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At such a distance, would the trajectory necessarily be a parabolical one?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It's not officially a parabolic because it's not the same on both sides, but it's -- for these rounds it would be almost parabolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Regardless of that, does that mean that there must have been optical visibility present if the intention is ascribed to this shooter, as well as an appropriate range for him to fire such a shot?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Yes. The shooter would have had to see the person he was -- the target he was shooting at, and there would be any kind of optical equipment present. Not necessarily on the weapon itself, but at least within -- nearby, in the form of binoculars.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. By looking at page 13, one can conclude that this distance excludes calibre 7.62 39 millimetres, and the wound that you haven't seen excluded the calibre larger than 7.62. Why did you take this roundabout course of action? Why didn't you take the documents and the slug and make your decision on that basis?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: There was no slug in the -- in the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there was a slug but that it was lost, as were medical documents, and that the father, the mother of the wounded girl said that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So what did you conclude then, that it might have been fired from the Baba Rock, or did you conclude that the shot definitely came from that location and that it can be used as proof in a legal sense?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: According to my findings, I would conclude that the shot originated from the -- in the direct vicinity of Baba Rock because that's the only location that there's a view of the incident site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What if the bullet was 7.62 39 millimetres? Where would the shot then have come from?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I would not know, because I did not see any possibilities for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, on the basis of what do you claim that it must have been a 7.9 millimetre bullet instead of a 7.62 millimetre? If it was a 60 -- if it was a 7.62x39 millimetres, then it could not have been fired from the distance of 920 metres; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It -- it would be very unlikely. It's at the most extreme range for which it would not be possible to set your sights for that distance. So there is a possibility, but it's very limited.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's conclude this subject now. Had this shot been fired by the Serbs from the Baba Rock, would be true only because there's a sole indication that it must have been a 7.9 calibre; however, there is no proof that this was the actual calibre of the bullet.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I did not conclude that it was a 7.9. I said it was within the group. There is two 7.62 bullets that might have been used or the 7.92. So there's a group of bullets that might have been used. Aside from that which I've already listed in the weapons ammunition, these are the military calibres. But hunting rifles also might have been used, and they use different rounds as well. But if they are military bullets or military-style bullets, these -- I believe these three bullets represent the group of bullets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, before this Tribunal had you ever appeared as an expert witness in any trials?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No. I've only appeared as an expert witness for -- in cases for the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tomorrow, if we succeed in opening certain documents, we will demonstrate that you should have been informed about the deployment, the confrontation, and the combat operations. So that would have led you to a conclusion that it was a stray 7.62 millimetre; is that correct? Mr. Van der Weijden, what is preventing you from saying that the bullet came from the Muslim-controlled territory? In other words, what is preventing you to allow for a possibility that this was a 7.62x39 millimetres, apart from the fact that the Serbs were not close enough?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I would refer back to page 15 of my report. On photo 2, this is the photo that I took that, in my view, offers the only possibility from where the shot might have originated from; and within that photo, Baba -- the arrow points to Baba Stijena, and that's the only location that I deem possible. So that's how I reached my conclusion that it's -- the bullet did not come from Muslim-controlled territory, even though I did not know where the Muslims were at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have this photo in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What does the arrow indicate here? As far as I can see, it is pointing to some foliage. And if this is Baba Stijena, then the distance could not have been more than 50 metres; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's just take a look. Just English or B/C/S, whatever, and let's zoom in. Further. Second -- second picture. Further. Further once again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. Where the arrow points directly is rock. And this is a picture that I've taken, of course, with a photo camera. And from the incident site, I observed the surroundings with binoculars, 6-power binoculars, which offers a better view. But for the picture to be the same quality as binoculars, it is difficult. But you don't see foliage where the arrow points but a gap between trees. And the light part that you see, that is rock.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, tell us, now, where -- where in this photo is the separation line, and where is the road that we saw a little earlier? And I will put it to you, Mr. Van der Weijden, if you look up, you can see some power line -- power lines there. I can tell you that this entire territory was under Muslim control, the entire area. And we weren't even close to that area.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I would not know, because this is -- I did not check for a separations line. I only checked for tactical possibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let's take a look at another incident, incident -- an incident on the 8th of October, 1994, which is under number 11 in the F schedule. Could you please look at this portion of your report. Can you tell us, in brief, the gist of this incident, the F11 incident. And for your information, Mr. Van der Weijden, the conclusion that it must have been -- that it was certainly fired from Baba Rock would not have been concluded even by a court in Bogujani [phoen] which is a place which is in the boondocks.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, the accused is now engaging in commentary rather than putting questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What was your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was simply for Mr. Van der Weijden's information, where, in fact, he should have been informed by the people who took him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But for now, could you just tell us in brief what the substance of case F11 is?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Well, the situation was as it's written on page 87, and I was -- as I was presented by the OTP, in which Alma Cutuna sustained injuries when the tram she was travelling in was fired upon and for which she recalls hearing bursts of fire, so multiple rounds, which shattered the glass and wounded her. There was apparently an expert investigation of the tram. The alleged shooting position was Grbavica. The calibre of -- the calibre weapons, since it was -- there were bursts of fire, I concluded that it most likely -- it will have been a machine-gun that had been used. And as for the origin of fire, when I visited the incident site, for me I concluded that some of the witness statements were contradictory to my findings. So I concluded different-wise as to the origin of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us more about the discrepancies. What are they?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Could you rephrase that question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The contradictions in some of the witnesses's statements and your conclusions, what was the gist? What did they consist in?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The inconsistencies, there was -- I was presented coordinates by the -- by the OTP, and I believe the coordinates that were matched to the incident sites, the exact incident sites -- and it's also -- that coordinate was used for the 360 video that was shot by the -- by the OTP, which I also had as evidence. Only when I matched the coordinate for the exact incident site it -- it made no -- it was contradictory to Grbavica. So I concluded that the location didn't match the witness statement of one -- of the victim. So I thought that was a mistake with the coordinates in the information that I received beforehand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And it didn't occur to you that there may have been an error in determining the incident -- or, rather, the fire position? So in other words, it was concluded that it must have been from Grbavica, come what may?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No, I did not automatically conclude that, because I took into account the -- within a short distance, the tram would also have been visible from the Jewish cemetery. It was clearly in view of that as well. So from those two areas, and if I then looked at the witness statements and taking into account that a tram moves while it's being fired upon, it's very difficult for the victims to exactly describe where they were hit -- when they were hit, because the realisation might come a little bit later. But then looking at the facts and the situation, then I conclude that Grbavica was the point of origin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the Prosecution provide the grid references of the origin of fire, or did they tell you that the origin of fire was at Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I was not given grid references of the origin of fire. They -- of course in the -- in the incident, it's already -- the facts that received of the OTP beforehand, the alleged shooting position already pointed to Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 87, you say the following: [In English] "Grbavica building (321m)." Alleged by whom? [Interpretation] Who determined the alleged position, that Grbavica was the alleged position?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I recall I read this in the witness reports but also in the -- it's probably also stated in the medical -- the expert examination of the tram. So in the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you attach those investigative materials produced by the Sarajevo police?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was the investigation accurate and complete? Was it satisfactory?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I cannot recall, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So what makes this a sniping incident, Mr. Van der Weijden?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I have never -- nowhere concluded that it was a sniper that fired -- fired in any of the incidents. This is just an incident that I was presented by the OTP and asked to look at it and determine if I could find what had been the origin of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Didn't the Muslim police -- or, rather, the Sarajevo police already indicate where the shooting had come from? Were you supposed to evaluate and assess the existing investigation reports done at the time of the incident, or were you supposed to just justify the findings and the allegations that the firing had been done by the Serbs and deliberately in order to harm the people on the tram?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Just as with the other incidents, I only took into account the existing investigation reports, if they were of technical assistance to me, in determining the point of origin. For the rest, I had nothing to do with justifying or denying anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me why, then, did you have to guess at the calibre? Weren't you provided the accurate calibres and rounds used? On page 87 we can see that, as in the other incidents, you first tried to determine the calibre that you didn't have any information on, but based on that calibre, you then go on to establish that it must have been fired by Serbs.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I don't think I've anywhere concluded that it was fired by Serbs. I cannot read it back in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the time of the incident, were any UNPROFOR members present on site? Can you remember?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I was not there at the time of the incident, so I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you recall or were you provided information to that effect that there were any TV reporters present on site?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Well, I'm aware that the Holiday Inn Hotel, which was a hotel where a lot of the news crews were staying, is in close vicinity of the incident site, but I would not know if the TV reporters would actually be present on site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Have you seen the footage that was produced by the official Sarajevo Television at the same time, at the time of the incident?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have 65 ter 1D04045, page 89, 14045. That's the English version. Page 89. I think in ERN page that would be 0629-5314.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: E-court page 90 of this expert report.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 90 of this report, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This one, Mr. Karadzic? Or the next page?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. That's not 65 ter -- no. Wait a minute. We need ERN ending in 314.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We are talking about different --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 14045. ERN 0629-5314. Can we pull that page up, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 88 in -- 89 in e-court. The previous page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think this is the right page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what these two photos actually represent? What do they depict?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You can see only one pictures.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Layout 1, Jewish cemetery v. Grbavica. Layout 1, Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They represent, in my view, this is the layout of the area around the incident site with green the actual incident site as located by the -- as mentioned in the report, and blue the location where I think the tram was -- was fired on. If I look down the street, the red cone or the -- the two cones, they represent, together with the slightly curved building below -- that building -- if the shooter would be on the left of the building, he would be able to have of a view on -- of the most right side of the upper cone, and if the shooter would be on the right side of the building, in the bottom, he would have view on the extreme left of the upper cone. So that represents the field of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And how did you determine where the tram was at the moment of the incident?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Because if the tram had been a little bit further, there is no situation that I can think of that the machine-gun was fired from the -- from the -- let's see what -- I think it was the left side. I believe in the -- the expert examination the location of the site of the tram was mentioned where the tram was hit, where the entries were, and that site was to the south. So if I would have a tram with -- facing -- that was fired upon from the south, there would be no possibilities for the machine-gun to be at, aside -- beside from down the street. And that would be represented by the two red cones.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Van der Weijden, if the tram had been hit while it was in a location a little forward or a little back of where you indicated that it was, then it could not have been fired from Grbavica; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So in other words, you are depicting this street as a shooting range, a slot through which one had to fire quickly because -- bearing in mind the speed of the movement of the tram.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: It would not be difficult, especially after being in position -- if it was indeed that building where I think the shots originated from, it would not be difficult to hit the tram, because you can hear the tram coming. So you can calculate over days what time it takes for the tram, from the time you hear it, to pass the intersection; and it would be just a question of pressing on the trigger to spray the -- to hit the tram.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And was this schematic produced on the basis of your conclusions and your findings, or did you draw your own conclusions based on something else; and if so, based on what?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: This is my schematic. I produced it myself, and it was based on my conclusions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have in e-court -- I don't know the 65 ter number, but that's the seventh map, photograph number 7 from the Karadzic binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we have the 65 ter number, Mr. Reid?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 21216. 65 ter 21216.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know what this photograph depicts, Mr. Van der Weijden? Can you recognise the street running between the School of Philosophy on the left-hand side and the museum on the right-hand side? And the photo was taken --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the position. From the Holiday Inn; interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can recognise the street, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is that the street along which one can actually hit the tram if fired -- if firing from Grbavica? Is that the street that you marked under the assumption that it was fired from Grbavica? You can also compare this to your photograph.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That is the same street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know what the buildings between the Holiday Inn and Grbavica are? And do you know where the School of Philosophy of the Sarajevo university and where the museum is and what we can see on top of the museum? Under whose control was this area between the Holiday Inn -- or, rather, the tram tracks and Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I know that the river was the dividing line for this area. So to the -- the Grbavica area would be under VRS control, and from the river to the Holiday Inn would be under Muslim control, or Bosnian control.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please indicate where the river is. Can you mark it, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: There would be the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please put number 1 there.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you agree with me that the building on the left-hand side is the School of Philosophy, the one close to the street?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: If it is this building, this is what I was told is the Faculty of Philosophy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you put number 2 there.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you see on the other side of the same street the museum complex, the buildings of the national museum?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I can see the buildings that were identified to me as being the museum, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please mark them.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now please draw a line to follow the bullet trajectory from the place where it was fired from up to the tram tracks.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I cannot draw a line because I do not know within the building that I marked the shooter actually was, so I would have to draw again the same two cones. It would be about this -- this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that the range should have been a little smaller because it encompasses one corner of the Faculty of Philosophy?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, this is only because -- because it's not easy to draw a good line. And furthermore, this is in perspective and not straight from the top, so it's not possible to determine the exact field of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Van der Weijden, did I understand you correctly that if the tram had been fired at beyond this cone then it could not have come from Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please put the date and your initials.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D647, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now have 65 ter document 21215.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this photograph, and is this viewed from the opposite direction with reference to the same place?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: More or less, because it's slightly from a different angle than the -- it's not straight across from the other photo. But they are the same buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you to draw these two identical cones, or as approximately as you can.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: That would be the cone. But, again, this is in perspective, so it doesn't -- it doesn't give the actual field of fire as it would be viewed from the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If the tram was hit on its right-hand side, would you agree in principle that it was not hit from north, rather, from the south, and south would mean 180 degrees? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: As I recall, because I -- I'm sorry I did not include the examination of the tram with my findings because they were lost somewhere, but as I recall, the tram was serving eastwards towards the town centre, and so it would have had its right side exposed to the south, to Grbavica. So it should -- should be hit -- if -- it was hit on the right side and not on the left side. I'm sorry if I misinterpreted that before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. I am not criticising you. Let us just make it precise. Does that allow for a possibility of 180 degrees instead of a full circle, i.e., 360 degrees?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Both the entry and exits -- exits of the bullets would be different. Not all the bullets would exit the tram on the other side, so it would be fairly easy to determine from which side the tram was fired -- was fired at.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But the physical obstacles demonstrate that only this small portion of the semicircle was possible to be achieved if the shots came from Grbavica. How far is the building where the supposed shooter was from the site incident? What is the figure that you cited?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I cited 321 metres from the centre of the building, measures with a laser rangefinder. And I waited till a tram passed to have -- have an exact reading to the tram line itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Speaking about this building, what was approximately the angle if the shot came from the top floor having in mind that there were eight floors, but the height was calculated as being 7 floor? What would the site angle be?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I would have to calculate, but it would be not much of influence because it's 321 metres away and then 35 metres high. So it's only a 1 in 10 declination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. We'll come to that. Is it acceptable to you that this is approximately 3.7 degrees?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I would have to calculate it, but that might be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What would be the descent angle of the bullet under such circumstances if the distance was 321 metres?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I would have to have access to the bullet trajectories of the bullets used. I could calculate it, but it would take time. I cannot take a -- take a guess now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When you prepared your report, did you make that calculation?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: No, I did not, because I did not deem it of importance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that if the site angle is around 4 degrees, the landing angle of the bullet would be around 5 degrees?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. I would have to calculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please prepare that for tomorrow. But do you agree that if it were 5 degrees, the bullet would ricochet?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I do not think for 5 degrees a bullet would ricochet because the 5 degrees will be only from the ground level instead of on the target. It will only deviate 5 degrees from straight on. So for this it will not ricochet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We are talking about an angle with respect to the ground; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: The degrees that you mentioned, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you were given this assignment, were you informed who was controlling the area between the building on the south as a possible shooting site and the tram and whose forces were deployed there? Why did you exclude the possibility that someone might have fired from that position as well?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: You imply the shooting from either the faculty or the museum properties?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the photographs. Do you see the Assembly building? Do you see it in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I think it is the big building on the right side with the dark roof. In the middle of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Can you please mark it.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And please put number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President. Can we clarify what date that that building was manufactured, if he's going to mark it. Sorry, was built I should say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it at issue or --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was built a long time before the war. It is still there, and its was there for the whole duration of the war. Is that a satisfactory answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So can you please now put a number 2 where the government building is.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I do not know what the government building is or where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark the high-rise building next to the Assembly building.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: This one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please put number 2.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And now the Faculty of Philosophy.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Number 3, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The museum.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Had you been informed that all these buildings, as you stated in your report that big buildings were used by shooters and snipers, were you informed that the top areas of these buildings had been occupied by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Not the exact location, but I was made aware of the fact that from the river to the big site where the tram lines are, that was Bosnian-controlled territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that the witnesses who were in the tram were unable to pinpoint an exact location because at the time when they were between the museum and the faculty they heard shots but they only noticed blood after the tram stopped?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: Well, they don't gave exact location of where they -- where the -- where exactly they were fired upon. It was only in the testimony that I read in the situation that she was approaching the stretch between the museum and the faculty. So she was approaching the crossroads, and after that something happened. It doesn't state if it happened after the crossing or even further down the track.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How do you explain that in the first incident relating to Anisa Pita the slug disappeared as well as the medical records, and in this case the expert report relating to the tram also went missing? How come this was not provided to you, and how do you explain that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think my time is up, and we shall continue tomorrow. Can you please tell me how much time I have left, and we will have to deal with this particular case just a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How much more with this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not more than 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Excuse me, you mean the F11 incident?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Weijden, could you kindly put the date of today and your signature.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you should conclude your

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will adjourn for today. We will give the number for this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit D648.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. 9.00 tomorrow morning.
